summary: Daniel Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, having also studied under Samli Mulkæo and Nalini Devdas. He served at Chiang Mai University (1999) and California State University, Chico (2003).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia and was attested as an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University in 2010.

Daniel Wojahn specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Leipzig and Oxford (DPhil 2019–2024), he has held posts at Leipzig, Oxford, Bonn (2024), and Vienna (2025), alongside working as a freelance indexer for Brill (2016–2020).

Daniel Wright (1833–1902) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews around 1849 to 1853 and later served as a physician at the British Residency in Nepal from 1866 to 1876.

Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Siena, and Paris Nanterre University. Her career includes posts at INALCO (2001–2003) and the CNRS as a senior researcher.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University (PhD). Her appointments include SOAS (2015–2020), the University of Turin (2021), and Iscte – University Institute of Lisbon (2023).

Daniela De Simone works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She earned degrees from Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, LSE, and Naples "L'Orientale". Her appointments include posts at UNESCO, the British Museum (2016–2020), and Ghent University (2021).

Daniele Cuneo, who taught Arinde L. Jonker, has held academic posts at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (both attested 2018). He is also attested as a faculty member at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001. During her academic training, she studied under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and teacher Ganesh U. Thite.
Danny M.C. Ching works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He has pursued his studies as a PhD student at Columbia University, attested in 2023 and 2026.
Danping Long is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, Long is attested as a doctoral student at both the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Danuta Stasik is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980) under Maria Byrski. In 1986, she took up a post at the University of Warsaw as Chair of South Asian Studies in the Faculty of Oriental Studies.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937), later serving as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1953 to 1992.

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi, Jai Narain Vyas University, and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1970–1974).

Daud Ali is a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1995–2008) before joining the University of Pennsylvania as Associate Professor in 2009.
David A. Dilworth is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968), and he later taught Steve Odin.

David A. Hall is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima and earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and later chaired a department at Montgomery College.

David Aberle (1918–2004) studied at Harvard University (~1937–1940), Columbia University (~1940–1950), and the University of New Mexico (~1941–1942). He later held an academic post at the University of British Columbia from around 1967 to 1983.
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London, where he completed his PhD under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and held positions at Rice University and Santa Clara University (attested 2005–2017).
